title: [recoverability] The transcript and mission restore drill runs daily (spawn-backup-restore-drill.timer, the bundle's environment, so its records reach the bundle's store) and judges the backup against its own record (transcripts.sha256 per file as bundled)
prompt:
Spawn, objective 149 [recoverability] (core line 4; projects-47's order and decisions of 2026-11-14, sync/scope-149-recorded-drills.md; 149b, the drill scratch's fd-held removal, follows as its own deleter objective): the transcript archive's and the mission repositories' restore drill runs every day, judges the backup against its own record, and records its verdict in the store the bundle records go to.

Why: the recovery north star (`recoverability.restores_passed` on /api/core-lines) counts 2 of 6. The Core lines rows "Transcript archive" and "Mission repositories" already read `backup.drilled.transcripts` and `backup.drilled.missions` (objective 104). But on live there is no such record in the last 14 days (projects-47's read, 2026-11-14): `spawn backup restore-drill` runs only by hand, and no unit runs it. Its verdict is also taken against live only: the bundle record names each transcript's size, not its bytes, so a restore cannot be checked without the live files.

Read first: crates/spawn-cli/src/backup.rs (`bundle`: the window, `transcripts.sizes`); crates/spawn-cli/src/backup/restore_drill.rs (`run`, `compare_transcripts`, `sha256_prefix`, `record_verdicts` through `store.backup_record`, the bundle's writer); deploy/systemd/spawn-backup-bundle.service and spawn-backup-verify.{service,timer}; deploy/backup/README.md (install, the drill); crates/spawn-postgres/sql/schema.sql `spawn_backup_record` (the drill record's fixed shape: unchanged by 149).

What changes:
(1) `spawn backup bundle` records each transcript's sha256 as bundled: `transcripts.sha256`, beside `transcripts.sizes`, maps every file in the window to the sha256 of its first `size` bytes, unchanged files too, so the newest record alone names every file a restore must give back. One more read of the window per bundle (about 522 MB on live, once a day). The record grows by about 80 bytes a file. backup.bundled has no shape check in spawn_backup_record; a refused bundle's record (`record_refusal`, it stored nothing) is unchanged.
(2) `spawn backup restore-drill` judges each restored transcript against that record before comparing with live:
- a restored file whose sha256 is not the one the newest record names, or a file the record sizes without a sha256, is a mismatch of the transcripts;
- the drill says "restore-drill: transcripts: <n> of <m> files as the newest record's sha256";
- a newest record bundled before 149 (no `transcripts.sha256`) is said ("the newest record names no per-file sha256 (bundled before objective 149): judged against live only") and judged against live as today, with no mismatch of its own;
- the comparison with live stays as it is (projects-47's (b)): a live transcript that grew since the bundle with the restored bytes as its first bytes is information ("grown since"), not a failure; a live transcript that differs inside the backed-up range, is shorter, is gone, or was written within the window and is in no bundle still fails.
- The records keep their types and their fixed shape (`{type, ok, reason, bundle, bundle_event_id, mismatches, duration_ms}`): ok true or false is the drill's passed or failed, and the rows already read them.
(3) The schedule: deploy/systemd/spawn-backup-restore-drill.service and .timer, user units shaped as spawn-backup-verify's:
- the timer at 05:30 daily (RandomizedDelaySec=15min, Persistent=true), after the 04:00 bundle and its retries, and the 05:00 dump drill;
- the service: Type=oneshot, ExecStart=%h/.local/share/spawn-rsi/bin/spawn backup restore-drill, and the bundle unit's EnvironmentFile and Environment lines exactly (spawn.env, SPAWN_WORKSPACE_ROOT, PATH, no_proxy), so the drill reads the bundle records from, and writes its records to, the store the bundle writes to; Restart=on-failure with RestartPreventExitStatus=1 2 (a failed drill is the record's and a person's; 2 cannot run), RestartSec=1h, TimeoutStartSec=1h, MemoryMax=1G, Nice=15, IOSchedulingClass=idle.
- deploy/backup/README.md: the schedule row, the install lines (`install -m 644 …` and `systemctl --user enable --now … spawn-backup-restore-drill.timer`), and the drill's text (the record check; "records nothing" corrected: it records its verdicts since 104).
Owner hold (projects-47, 2026-11-14): the drill removes its own restored transcript copies with its scratch directory, and the owner rule is that transcripts are never deleted; the owner is asked (through lead-mac). Until the owner answers, no drill runs, by hand or by timer. Then: The timer is installed and enabled only after 149b passes and lands; until then the drill runs only by hand, attended, by the lead (rev-g's F1 on 149 R1, accepted by projects-47): until 149b the drill removes its scratch directory by name after a check, which is no removal to run unattended every day. The README says so, gives the by-hand command (the bundle's environment, so the records reach the bundle's store), and keeps the timer's install lines apart, for after 149b. No deploy step installs the units.

Writes and deletion (unchanged by 149; 149b changes the removal):
- The drill writes only into its own scratch directory, `spawn-restore-drill-<pid>-<hex>`, mode 700, made new under --into (default /data/tmp; never under $HOME, $SPAWN_LIVE or the workspace root, symlinks resolved), and its two records. Live files and repositories are only read.
- Its only deletion is that directory, at the end: today's `fs::remove_dir_all` of the path it made, after checking the name is a drill's, its parent the one it was made in, and its (dev, ino) the one made. That is the name-based shape of cc-astra's A58 on 145, so the drill runs only by hand, attended, until 149b, which keeps the directory's fd from its creation and empties it through that fd (rev-g, then cc-astra), passes and lands.
- A run killed part way leaves its directory under /data/tmp; the next run never touches it.

What stays as it is: the bundle's contents and keys, verify, the dump drill, every record shape in the store, the Core lines rows (core-lines.json is the lead's), the drill's exit codes and its --into, --keep and --root.

Tests (unit, crates/spawn-cli/src/backup/restore_drill.rs):
- restored_transcripts_are_judged_against_the_records_sha256: the bytes as bundled pass ("2 of 2"); the same size with other bytes fails, named; a file the record sizes without a sha256 fails; a record without the map is said, with no mismatch.
- a_prefix_hash_is_of_the_first_bytes_only: the recorded hash of a grown file is the hash of its bundled bytes.

Files: crates/spawn-cli/src/backup.rs, crates/spawn-cli/src/backup/restore_drill.rs, deploy/systemd/spawn-backup-restore-drill.service (new), deploy/systemd/spawn-backup-restore-drill.timer (new), deploy/backup/README.md. No other open objective touches them.
Size: about 200 lines, under the 300-line rule.
- Code and doc comments: +77 −1 (backup.rs +9; restore_drill.rs +68 −1).
- Units: +38 (spawn-backup-restore-drill.service 27, .timer 11).
- README: +14 −5.
- Tests: +67 (restore_drill.rs).

Acceptance: rsi/scenarios/149.sh, black box, with SPAWN_BIN and a test database of its own, under a scratch HOME and GNUPGHOME, against 104's local R2 stand-in. The bundle and the first drill run as systemd runs them: the checkout's unit file's ExecStart (%h the scratch HOME, `bin/spawn` a link to SPAWN_BIN), in an environment of the unit's EnvironmentFile (a spawn.env in the scratch HOME naming the database, R2 and the key) and Environment lines only, every SPAWN_*, PG* and git setting unset; the drill's ExecStart is given --into a scratch parent, so nothing goes to /data/tmp. It checks:
(1) the bundle unit's run records backup.bundled with transcripts.sha256: for every file its sizes name, the sha256 of the live file's first size bytes;
(2) the drill unit's run passes, says "<n> of <n> files as the newest record's sha256", records backup.drilled.transcripts and backup.drilled.missions ok in the bundle's store, naming the bundle unit's record, leaves no scratch directory, and changes nothing live (every file of the archive and the sources, by path, size and sha256);
(3) live moves on append-only (a transcript grows, a commit is pushed): the drill passes, the grown file counted;
(4) a live transcript changed inside its backed-up range (same size, one byte other): exit 1, transcripts ok false with a mismatch, missions ok true;
(5) a newest bundle record without transcripts.sha256 (the same record, inserted as the store writes control records): the drill passes, says so, and judges that record;
(6) a newest record naming, for one file, the sha256 of other bytes, while the backup and live agree: exit 1, transcripts ok false with that one mismatch, named; missions ok true. Only the record check can fail this case.
(7) no secret in a record or the output.
On the base (live main 22d0fdde), 149.sh exits 1 at its first check: "(1) the bundle record's sha256 of agent_supervisor/….jsonl: expected <sha> (its first 264786 bytes), got none".

Proof (rev-e-96, sync/obj-149/149-proof.txt; R1 s149 78ef4b48 on 22d0fdde, then R2 40f4715d, text only: the README, the module doc and this prompt (rev-g's F1); after R2, fmt --all, clippy -D warnings, the build and 149.sh pass again, s149out3; run.sh's output s149out1, mutrun.sh's s149out1, rerun.sh's s149out2 with 149.sh as published):
- 149.sh: the base exits 1 twice, at (1). The throwaway exits 0 five times: twice before (6) was added, and three times with it. 104.sh, 114.sh and deploy/backup/test-restore-drill.sh still pass.
- --list for spawn-cli and spawn-postgres against the base: 0 missing, 2 new tests only.
- clippy -D warnings is clean (spawn-cli, spawn-postgres, all targets), and `cargo fmt --all --check` is clean. The backup unit tests pass (57).
- Eight mutants (mut-149.py), each applied alone, each killed:
  - by 149.sh: no-hash-recorded (1), record-check-skipped (2), unit-no-envfile (2), unit-other-command (2), prefix-hash-whole (3), mismatch-dropped (6);
  - by 149.sh and a unit test: record-check-always-same ((6) and restored_transcripts_are_judged_against_the_records_sha256);
  - by a unit test only: missing-sha-ignored (restored_transcripts_are_judged_against_the_records_sha256). Every record the binary writes names a sha256 for every file it sizes, so the scenario never meets a record without one.
- In the first mutant round mismatch-dropped survived: a corrupted backup also differs from live, so live caught every record mismatch the scenario made. Check (6) was added to 149.sh for it and kills it.

Verified by (after the owner's answer on the drill's restored transcript copies; until then no drill runs):
- After the PASS and the landing, projects-47 runs the drill by hand, attended, with the bundle's environment (deploy/backup/README.md's command), and reads its output.
- That run writes backup.drilled.transcripts and backup.drilled.missions on live; the lead reads them (ok, reason).
- Within a day of that run, /api/core-lines `recoverability.restores_passed` reads 4 (of 6), and sync/recovery.md's two rows carry the pass. The lead posts both in sync.
- The timer is installed and enabled only after 149b passes and lands; until then the drill runs only by hand, attended, by the lead. Each by-hand pass counts for 7 days.
